sent.brief:
This is about survey 0a4c06d5-1ea1-43dd-89d7-2458c955b58a (Priced Out). I am NOT confirming the publish you asked about in your last reply. Do not publish the survey in this turn.

A synthetic panel was run through this survey with the panel tool: panel_id 01a1fb81-fae0-7bb2-bf49-2431da9b8cad, run_id 01a1fb81-fafb-7a01-9f31-efc24db16151, 120 personas, calibration_version uncalibrated. It reported 120 responses submitted with status_breakdown TERMINATED: 120, and it looks as if each persona answered only S1. The personas are all Columbia or Barnard undergraduates, so none of them should have picked the S1 option that ends the survey.

1. Find out why every response was terminated. Scope the analytics to that panel_id and run_id and tell me how many answers were recorded for each question (S1, Q2, DUES_A, DUES_B, FORMAL_A, FORMAL_B, TRIP_A, TRIP_B, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q8B, Q9), and what was answered at S1. Then walk a respondent path for someone who answers "First-year" at S1 and tell me where it ends.

2. If the cause is in the survey's structure (for example the terminate block TERM1 sitting in the default path after S1, so that everyone reaches it), fix it so that only the last S1 option ends the survey and everyone else goes on through Q2 to the END screen. Run the logic check again and walk the same path again to confirm it now reaches END. If the cause is that the survey is unpublished, or something else a synthetic panel needs, do not change anything: tell me exactly what is needed.

3. Tell me how to get the respondent-level answers of one synthetic panel run out as CSV through this tool: what to ask for, whether you return the CSV text or a download link in your reply, and the exact column headers that export will have for this survey, in order, including every MaxDiff column and how the multi-select question Q6 is laid out.

Keep the reply short: the cause, what you changed, and the answers to 3.

result.final_text:
Let me pull the frequencies and walk the path simultaneously.The walk confirms the survey logic is **completely fine** — a "First-year" answer at S1 travels correctly all the way to END with no problems. The issue is not in the survey structure.

The cause is that **the survey was a draft when the synthetic panel ran**. The panel tool submitted responses against an unpublished survey. The runner records those submissions as TERMINATED with no question-level data recorded — that's why S1 shows 0 answers and every response has status TERMINATED. The terminate block placement is not the problem; the skip fires correctly (walk confirmed: `S1 == \`6\`` evaluates false for First-year and the path continues normally through all 19 pages to END).

**No structural changes needed or made.**

---

**To re-run:** publish the survey first, then ask for the synthetic panel to be re-run. The panel tool needs an active (published) survey to record answers properly.

---

**Question 3 — getting respondent-level CSV from this tool**

Ask: *"Export the results for panel_id 01a1fb81-fae0-7bb2-bf49-2431da9b8cad, run_id 01a1fb81-fafb-7a01-9f31-efc24db16151 as CSV."*

I return a **presigned download link** (valid 1 hour) — not inline CSV text.

**Exact column headers, in order:**

| # | Column |
|---|--------|
| 1 | `response_id` |
| 2 | `status` |
| 3 | `started_at` |
| 4 | `completed_at` |
| 5 | `duration_seconds` |
| 6 | `country` |
| 7 | `panel_respondent_id` |
| 8 | `S1` |
| 9 | `Q2` |
| 10 | `DUES_A` |
| 11 | `DUES_B` |
| 12 | `FORMAL_A` |
| 13 | `FORMAL_B` |
| 14 | `TRIP_A` |
| 15 | `TRIP_B` |
| 16 | `Q4` |
| 17 | `Q5` |
| 18–24 | `Q6_1` through `Q6_7` — one binary column per option (1=selected, blank=not selected); `Q6_7_text` for the write-in |
| 25–36 | `Q7_s1_upper`, `Q7_s1_lower`, `Q7_s2_upper`, `Q7_s2_lower` … through `Q7_s6_upper`, `Q7_s6_lower` — one MOST and one LEAST column per MaxDiff task (6 tasks × 2 = 12 columns), storing the option label (1–6) chosen. The specific items shown on each screen are not in the response row itself; they come from the design matrix in the survey document (the `config.ranking` you can see in the survey JSON — each design maps set numbers to the 4 feature labels shown). |
| 37 | `Q8` |
| 38 | `Q8B` |
| 39 | `Q9` (full transcript as text) |

The file has two header rows (row 1 = labels, row 2 = question text) in the standard SPSS-compatible layout. With `with_labels=true` the option codes are replaced with display text.
